note: Seven sources to start the list. Every claim's evidence status is null: Karl has not rated them. 'howRead' is null where nobody has confirmed whether the source was read in full. The first three are cited on Home. Most were read by Claude in summary only.

references.shortCitation: Mullainathan and Shafir, Scarcity: Why Having Too Little Means So Much (2013)
references.citation: Mullainathan, S. and Shafir, E. (2013). Scarcity: Why Having Too Little Means So Much.

claims.claim: When survival is in question, attention narrows to the immediate.
claims.note: Check the replication record of this research before rating it as established evidence.

references.citation: Ryan, R. and Deci, E. (2000). Self-determination theory and the facilitation of intrinsic motivation, social development, and well-being. American Psychologist.

references.citation: Ostrom, E. (1990). Governing the Commons. Cambridge University Press.

claims.claim: Communities can govern shared resources well, under the right conditions, without central direction.
claims.note: Claude chose this source for the claim. Karl to confirm.

references.shortCitation: Ostrom, A Polycentric Approach for Coping with Climate Change (2009)
references.citation: Ostrom, E. (2009). A Polycentric Approach for Coping with Climate Change. World Bank Policy Research Working Paper.

claims.claim: Action on a shared global problem need not wait for a single global agreement.

references.citation: Keohane, R. and Victor, D. (2011). The Regime Complex for Climate Change. Perspectives on Politics.

references.citation: Hayek, F. A. (1945). The Use of Knowledge in Society. American Economic Review, 35(4).

claims.claim: The information needed to run a complex system is spread among the people in it. No center can gather it all.
